failures: A metadata-only repair was not adopted, so the final validation stayed not-run even though the repaired action had a usable entry and no additional file diff.

A file-plus-metadata repair was rejected as a scope violation because the allowed paths came only from the stale action declaration and ignored the actual candidate path; the repaired action was not merged.

implementation.feedbackContract: Each failed action now carries baselineAction, candidateAction, candidateDiff, originalIntent, diagnostics and relevant files. Candidate diff paths come from an engine filesystem comparison, not self-reported changedPaths.
implementation.scope: Repair scope includes the failed action's declared/local references plus candidate diff paths not claimed by another action; unrelated independent paths remain outside the scope.
implementation.constrainedMerge: Only validated repaired metadata for failed action ids is merged. The original action set, root cause, file-change summary and independent actions remain authoritative; malformed or out-of-scope repair entries do not add or delete actions.
implementation.validation: The merged action set is revalidated before execution. A repaired action is explicitly in executeActionIds even when changedPathsSincePrior is empty; unaffected actions reuse a binding-matched observation.
implementation.packageClosure: Final report, history entry and exported package use the merged repaired action set and the repaired workspace snapshot.

cases: file-plus-action repair with an omitted independent action in the repair submission
existing independent repair, shared dependency revalidation and shared-group rollback regressions

claimBoundary: Development evidence only. C4 proves constrained local repair adoption for the designed metadata-only and file-plus-metadata cases, including final validation/history/package binding. It does not establish the new-program natural-consumption chain, general optimizer reliability, behavior improvement, prospective readiness, held-out performance, or human savings.
